edit.description: the `mkdir` moves from the constructor to `wake`, and every read takes an absent directory as the empty baton
the seam with the queue's other help-page entries: a read verb's page stops carrying a write refusal its process can no longer take
the `status` and `render` sections stop naming the directory as a read verb's one filesystem effect
the reads over an absent directory and `wake`'s own creation
the second-root case's empty `awake/` comes from a real writer that still plants one

summary: A read verb's `new Baton` mkdirs `awake/`, so `status` and `render` write under a state root the spec says reading the baton creates nothing beneath
acceptance: constructing the baton writes nothing; the first `wake` creates the directory, and the flag reads take its absence as the empty baton, so `flume status` prints `hibernating` over a state root it leaves untouched and `flume render` keeps its no-write claim — and the `StateRootWriteError` that `mkdir` raised moves to `wake` with it, so no page states a refusal the verb's process can no longer take
tests: constructing the baton creates no awake-flag directory
the first wake creates the awake-flag directory the constructor no longer makes
flume status over a state root with no awake-flag directory prints hibernating and writes nothing
notes: Operator's ruling; the constructor pin retires with it. Verified: `mkdirUnderStateRoot` at `src/Baton.ts:87`, `awake()` (`:92`) readdirs the dir, `wake()` (`:140`) writes the flag alone. Copies: `docs/CLI.md:33`, `:221`. The blocker it waited on — THE-VERB-PAGES-NAME-THE-STATE-ROOT-WRITE-REFUSAL, which added that refusal to every verb reachable from `new Baton` — shipped at 1615b10f, so this narrowing now lands on top of it.
